entries.respiratory.airway.trachea: The trachea (windpipe) is a flexible tube held open by C-shaped cartilage rings. It carries air from the larynx to the two main bronchi, dividing at the carina.
entries.respiratory.airway.main-bronchus.right: The right main bronchus is shorter, wider and more vertical than the left.
entries.respiratory.airway.main-bronchus.left: The left main bronchus is longer and more horizontal than the right, and passes beneath the arch of the aorta.
Lobar and segmental bronchi supplying the right upper lobe.
Lobar and segmental bronchi supplying the right middle lobe.
Lobar and segmental bronchi supplying the right lower lobe.
entries.respiratory.airway.bronchial-tree.left.u: Lobar and segmental bronchi supplying the left upper lobe, including the lingula.
entries.respiratory.airway.bronchial-tree.left.l: Lobar and segmental bronchi supplying the left lower lobe.
entries.respiratory.lung.right.upper-lobe: The right upper lobe has three bronchopulmonary segments: apical, posterior and anterior.
entries.respiratory.lung.right.middle-lobe: The right middle lobe has two bronchopulmonary segments: lateral and medial.
entries.respiratory.lung.right.lower-lobe: The right lower lobe has a superior segment and four basal segments: medial, anterior, lateral and posterior.
entries.respiratory.lung.left.upper-lobe: The left upper lobe includes the lingula, the left counterpart of the right middle lobe.
entries.respiratory.lung.left.lower-lobe: The left lower lobe has a superior segment and the basal segments.
entries.respiratory.vessel.pulmonary-artery.righ: Pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. Shown in blue by atlas convention.
entries.respiratory.vessel.pulmonary-artery.left: Pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. Shown in blue by atlas convention.
entries.respiratory.vessel.pulmonary-vein.right: Pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. Shown in red by atlas convention.
entries.respiratory.vessel.pulmonary-vein.left: Pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. Shown in red by atlas convention.
entries.respiratory.diaphragm: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle separating the thorax from the abdomen. It is the main muscle of inspiration and is supplied by the phrenic nerve.
entries.skeletal.skull: The skull protects the brain and forms the framework of the face.
entries.skeletal.mandible: The mandible is the lower jaw, the only freely movable bone of the skull.
entries.skeletal.thoracic-cage.sternum: The sternum (breastbone) has three parts: the manubrium, the body and the xiphoid process.
entries.skeletal.thoracic-cage.costal-cartilages: Costal cartilages connect the upper ribs to the sternum and give the chest wall flexibility.
entries.skeletal.vertebral-column.sacrum: The sacrum is formed by fused vertebrae and joins the spine to the pelvis.
entries.skeletal.shoulder-girdle.clavicle.right: The clavicle (collarbone) links the sternum to the scapula.
entries.skeletal.shoulder-girdle.clavicle.left: The clavicle (collarbone) links the sternum to the scapula.
entries.skeletal.shoulder-girdle.scapula.right: The scapula (shoulder blade) lies on the posterior chest wall.
entries.skeletal.shoulder-girdle.scapula.left: The scapula (shoulder blade) lies on the posterior chest wall.
entries.skeletal.pelvic-girdle.hip-bone.right: The hip bone joins the sacrum and its pair to form the pelvis.
entries.skeletal.pelvic-girdle.hip-bone.left: The hip bone joins the sacrum and its pair to form the pelvis.

There are twelve pairs of ribs. Ribs 1 to 7 attach directly to the sternum through costal cartilage, ribs 8 to 10 attach indirectly, and ribs 11 and 12 are free-ended.
There are seven cervical vertebrae, supporting the head and neck.
There are twelve thoracic vertebrae. Each articulates with a pair of ribs.
There are five lumbar vertebrae, the largest of the mobile spine.
